claim_ceiling: Minimal energy-budgeted integrity control distinguishing passive relaxation, fixed-rate repair and proportional feedback. No claim of biological life, autonomy in nature, intelligence or consciousness.

source_basis.relation_to_control_theory: Known-input single-state control system with exact passive exponential decay, bounded actuator and explicit work/energy accounting.

controller_modes.rule: no repair actuator; exact passive exponential decay only
constant repair rate independent of observed integrity error, bounded by max_repair_rate and target headroom
repair rate = gain_per_time * max(target_integrity - integrity_before_repair, 0), bounded by max_repair_rate and target headroom

cases.purpose: Test whether the controller expends repair energy when no integrity deficit exists.

expected.integrity_after: less than or equal to initial; only passive decay applies

cases.purpose: Compare passive persistence against energy-consuming error-feedback repair under the same disturbance.

expected.passive: integrity remains below the target and continues passive decay; no repair or repair-energy use
expected.feedback: integrity returns to target if the available energy budget permits; restoration is accompanied by positive repair work and energy expenditure

cases.purpose: Determine whether repair effort scales with perturbation magnitude or is merely a fixed scripted response.

expected.fixed_rate: same requested effort for both perturbation sizes, subject to target headroom
expected.feedback: requested effort scales with integrity error; for these values, the large-deficit request is four times the small-deficit request before common rate/energy clipping

cases.purpose: Test whether apparent recovery depends on the feedback controller.
cases.expected: repair ceases after controller knockout; passive decay continues

cases.purpose: Test whether repair is actually energy constrained rather than a free state reset.
Test the difference between finite stored reserve and sustained environmental energy intake.
cases.expected: repair consumes only the finite initial reserve; once depleted, unmet repair grows and integrity cannot be restored

cases.purpose: Test the controller against a pre-registered perturbation sequence not used to set its gain or fixed-rate baseline.
cases.expected: This is a deterministic, pre-registered out-of-calibration stress sequence, not a random-seed experiment. Report recovery, energy limitation and residual integrity for every step; do not infer learning from robust feedback under a fixed known control law.

anti_leakage: All steps within one trajectory remain in one split.
All runs with the same parameter set and seed family remain grouped.
Report fixed-rate and feedback controllers on identical perturbation and energy-input sequences.
Do not treat time steps as independent experimental systems.
A successful controller does not establish learning, adaptation, life or agency unless those properties are independently operationalized.

reproducibility.seed: only the unseen perturbation sequence uses sequence_seed; core state transitions are deterministic
